haiku-low.q1: If the unfiltered reports.row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the CSV is returned directly in the response. Above 10,000, an export record is created, a background job runs, and the user gets an emailed 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The existing active row is returned as 200 with already_running true, and nothing new is enqueued. The page shows that export's filters. Rows stuck over 3 hours are failed and replaced.
haiku-low.q3: The signed link works for 24 hours (86,400 s). The existing bucket rule deletes the stored file after 7 days. Unfinished multipart uploads are discarded after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with waits of 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure the row is marked failed and the user gets a report_export_failed email with no link. A done export is not marked failed.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica, never the primary. The report_exports metadata table lives on the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary database. The page polls the status endpoint every 5 s while queued or running. On reopening, it fetches the caller's most recent export.
haiku-low.q7: It streams: reads 5,000 rows per keyset page and uploads 8 MB multipart parts, so peak memory is about 20 to 30 MB. Estimated duration is well under the 1800 s timeout, with a target under 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible until complete_multipart, and the failed upload is aborted best-effort. The next attempt starts from scratch with a new upload and overwrites the same key. Progress is not kept between attempts.
haiku-low.q9: The raw filters and cols query string is stored in the report_exports row's query_string column. The job payload holds only export_id, and the job loads query_string from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A database unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the database, not application code, enforces it.
haiku-low.q11: Before the email, the row is set to done and a 24-hour signed URL is generated. On a rerun, a failed row returns, and a done row with notified_at returns. A done row without notified_at only sends the email.
haiku-low.q12: No bytes are sent until the file is complete, so the user never gets a truncated file. Any query error or the 45 s deadline returns 503, and the page shows try again.

sonnet.q1: It reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total) from the replica. 10,000 or fewer: small path, the POST response itself is the CSV file (200 text/csv attachment). Above 10,000: large path, an export record is created and a background job queued; the user gets 202 {export_id, status queued}, then later an email with a 24-hour download link. A heavily filtered view of a big report still takes the large path.
sonnet.q2: The insert hits the unique partial index (user, report where queued/running) and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; nothing new is enqueued. The existing row is returned as 200 {export_id, status, already_running: true, query_string}, and the page shows its filters (which may differ from the current view). Exceptions: if the active row's updated_at is over 3 hours old it is marked failed (no email) and a new insert is retried; if its job_id is null and it is over 2 minutes old, it is re-enqueued.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours (86,400 s). The existing bucket rule deletes the stored object after 7 days (unfinished uploads are discarded after 24 h). No cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s then 300 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure runs once: sets status=failed with a short error and finished_at (freeing the unique index), and emails report_export_failed with no link. The page shows failed on the next poll or visit. Exception: if the row is already done (only the email failed), it is not marked failed; it is logged, and the user sees done but has no link.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only. Never the primary and never a fallback to it; a replica error is a failure. (The report_exports table lives on the primary but holds metadata, not report data.)
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row in the primary database (status queued/running/done/failed). The page learns by calling GET /api/reports/{id}/export on page load, after a click that returns a status, and polling every 5 s while queued or running. It returns the caller's most recent export (404 if none). Nothing is kept on the client, so a returning user sees the same state from the server row. Failed polls keep the last state and retry; polling stops at done or failed.
sonnet.q7: It streams the file as a multipart upload. It reads 5,000 rows per replica query using keyset paging, encodes CSV into a buffer, and uploads a part whenever the buffer reaches 8 MB. At the end it uploads the remainder as the last part, then calls complete_multipart. Peak memory is about 20-30 MB (one 8 MB buffer plus a page), far under 512 MB. That is about 113 parts and about 400 queries, needing only about 0.5 MB/s against the 1800 s timeout (target under 10 minutes, to be measured).
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible, because the object does not exist until complete_multipart. On a caught exception the job makes a best-effort abort_multipart and sets the row back to queued with the error. After a timeout or worker death the orphaned upload is discarded by the 24 h bucket rule and the row stays running. The queue keeps no progress, so the next attempt starts from scratch: a new upload_id, a fresh read from the beginning (no resume), and the same object key, which it overwrites.
sonnet.q9: They are stored as the raw query_string (filters and cols from the page URL) in the report_exports row on the primary. The job is enqueued with a payload of only {export_id} (filters could exceed the 64 KB limit). The worker loads the row and parses query_string with the Row API parser.
sonnet.q10: The database: a unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') on report_exports, used with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. It is not enforced by application code. The second request gets the first row back.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have succeeded and the row must be set to status=done with finished_at; then a signed URL is made and the email sent, and then notified_at is set. If the queue runs the job again: a failed row returns immediately; done with notified_at set returns immediately (duplicate delivery); done with notified_at null skips the build and only sends the email, with a fresh URL. Two workers running the same export at once is not locked; the last complete_multipart wins.
sonnet.q12: No bytes are sent until the file is complete, so the user never gets a truncated file. Any query error returns 503. The 45 s deadline also returns 503, as does finding more than 10,000 rows (a stale count, 503 'try again'). Nothing is kept: no job, no table row, nothing in storage.
